Request password recovery

Source: R/reset.R
aa_request_password_reset.Rd

Finds a user by login or email, creates a one-time token and calls settings$send_reset(email, link, login) to send an email with the link. Only the token hash stays in the database. The user's previous unused links stop working.

Usage

aa_request_password_reset(conn, identifier, settings = aa_settings())

Arguments

conn

A connection to the SQLite database (DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ...)).

identifier

The login or email the user entered.

settings

Settings, the result of aa_settings() with reset_enabled = TRUE.

Value

A list (invisibly): sent (TRUE if the email was sent), reason ("sent", "disabled", "no_user", "no_email", "blocked", "throttled" or "send_failed") and login (the found login or NA).

Details

No email is sent if the user does not exist, has no email, is blocked by an administrator, or a limit is exceeded (reset_max_per_hour per user, reset_max_per_minute overall). The function result is meant for the journal: the user should be shown the same answer in every case, so that it is impossible to find out which logins and addresses exist.

An error in send_reset does not abort the function but is returned as send_failed: the token is consumed in that case.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("RSQLite", quietly = TRUE)) {
  conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")
  aa_init_db(conn)
  aa_create_first_admin(conn, "boss", "boss-password")
  aa_set_email(conn, "boss", "boss@example.com")

  settings <- aa_settings(
    reset_enabled  = TRUE,
    reset_base_url = "https://apps.example.com/my_app",
    send_reset = function(email, link, login) message("Link for ", login, ":
    ", link)
  )
  aa_request_password_reset(conn, "boss", settings)$reason
  aa_request_password_reset(conn, "nobody", settings)$reason
  DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)
}
#> Link for boss:
#>     https://apps.example.com/my_app/?reset=d42245ea46f6d300e3f0fc132535414bae2edd3ea9e7e7e328d2910023d4622f
